page_title: Command-Tab That Restores Minimized Windows – Command Reopen

summary.name: Command Reopen
summary.one_liner: A paid macOS utility that keeps the built-in Command-Tab but restores a minimized window (or opens a new one) when you switch to an app.
keywords: open new window when switching app
use_cases: Restore minimized windows when switching apps with Cmd+Tab
Use Command-Tab on company-managed Macs without granting permissions
Avoid replacing the native app switcher with a third-party one
Open a new window automatically for apps that have none open
summary.what_it_does: Command Reopen keeps the native macOS Command-Tab and changes what happens after you pick an app: if the app has a minimized window, it comes back, and if the app has no windows, it asks the app to open a new one, like clicking its Dock icon. It does not restore closed windows, documents, or tabs. It does not add window previews or a window grid; the page points to AltTab for that. It requires no Accessibility, Screen Recording, or other permissions, and runs in the Mac App Store sandbox. The source is on GitHub, and the free GitHub build is one version behind the App Store release, which updates automatically.
notable: Keeps the native Command-Tab instead of replacing it with a new switcher
Requires no Accessibility or Screen Recording permissions
Open source; source on GitHub, App Store build uses the same code
Sandboxed, notarized App Store version with automatic updates
caveats: Paid after a 2-day free trial: $9.99 one-time for the full app
Free GitHub build is one version behind the App Store release and does not update automatically
